message.content: In this repo (/work), find the source code implementing the ingest queue / sample store buffer (likely named IngestQueue or similar, related to "in-memory per-series sample store" per recent commit history). I need to know: what does the code actually do when the queue/buffer is full and a new sample arrives? Does it drop the oldest buffered item and accept the new one, or does it reject/refuse the incoming new sample and keep what it has? Quote the exact relevant code (file path + line numbers) and any comments explaining the behavior. Also check if there's a `dropped` counter or similar metric. Also search for any existing overflow/queue-related decision docs or comments mentioning "reject" or "drop oldest" or "drop newest". Report concisely with file:line references.

content.text:
## Findings

**Component:** `IngestQueue` in `/work/src/ingest.ts:38-73` (introduced in commit `3fee818` "feat: bounded ingest queue and wire-line parser"). There's also `MemoryStore` in `/work/src/store.ts` (per-series bucket, commit `77d6b32`) which has its own, separate overflow policy.

### Behavior on overflow: drops the OLDEST item, accepts the new one

`/work/src/ingest.ts:32-56`:
```
32 /**
33  * A bounded FIFO buffer between the wire and the store.
34  *
35  * Overflow drops the *oldest* sample, not the newest: under sustained pressure
36  * a recent picture beats a stale one.
37  */
38 export class IngestQueue {
39   private buffer: Sample[] = [];
40   private dropped = 0;
41   private readonly capacity: number;
...
50   push(sample: Sample): void {
51     this.buffer.push(sample);
52     while (this.buffer.length > this.capacity) {
53       this.buffer.shift();
54       this.dropped += 1;
55     }
56   }
```

So `push()` always appends the new sample first, then evicts from the front (`shift()`) until back within capacity — i.e. the incoming sample is always accepted, and the oldest buffered sample(s) are discarded to make room. The new sample is never rejected.

The explicit design rationale is the doc comment at lines 35-36: *"Overflow drops the oldest sample, not the newest: under sustained pressure a recent picture beats a stale one."*

### `dropped` counter / metric

- Private counter: `/work/src/ingest.ts:40` — `private dropped = 0;`
- Incremented on each eviction: `/work/src/ingest.ts:54` — `this.dropped += 1;`
- Public accessor: `/work/src/ingest.ts:69-72`:
```
69  /** How many samples overflow has discarded since construction. */
70  droppedCount(): number {
71    return this.dropped;
72  }
```
- Surfaced in the CLI/service output at `/work/src/index.ts:53`: `` `${series.length} series, ${service.queue.droppedCount()} dropped\n` ``

### Related test confirming behavior

`/work/test/ingest.test.ts:47-57`, `"drops the oldest sample on overflow"`: pushes values `[1,2,3]` into a capacity-2 queue, then asserts `drain()` yields `[2, 3]` (i.e., the oldest, `1`, was dropped, the newest was kept) and `droppedCount() === 1`.

### Router comment explaining why queue overflow (not store overflow) matters

`/work/src/router.ts:56-58`:
```
56  // Buffered, not stored: the queue is what absorbs a burst, and `tick()`
57  // is what moves a sample into the store. A write that went straight to
58  // the store would make the queue's overflow policy unreachable.
```

### The separate store-side overflow policy (also drop-oldest, per series)

`/work/src/store.ts:1-6` (class doc) and `28-33` (`put`):
```
1  /**
2   * In-memory sample storage, one sorted bucket per series.
3   *
4   * Deliberately not durable: this is a bounded in-memory buffer over a recent
5   * window — nothing is forwarded anywhere, and nothing reads it back.
6   */
...
28    const at = insertionPoint(bucket, sample.at);
29    bucket.splice(at, 0, sample);
30    if (bucket.length > this.maxPerSeries) {
31      bucket.splice(0, bucket.length - this.maxPerSeries);
32    }
```
This also always inserts the new sample (in timestamp order, not necessarily at the end) then trims from the front of the per-series bucket — same drop-oldest/accept-newest policy, but `MemoryStore` has no `dropped` counter of its own; only `prune()` (`/work/src/store.ts:47-60`) reports a removal count, for time-based pruning, not overflow.

Config doc reinforcing the policy: `/work/src/config.ts:8`:
```
8  /** Hard cap on samples held per series before the oldest are dropped. */
```

### No "reject" / "drop newest" policy found anywhere

A repo-wide search for "reject", "drop oldest", "drop newest", "dropped", "overflow" (excluding node_modules) found no decision doc or comment indicating rejection of new samples or dropping-newest; all matches are consistent with the drop-oldest/accept-newest policy described above (plus unrelated "rejects ..." test names for input *validation* failures in `/work/test/validate.test.ts` and `/work/test/ingest.test.ts` lines 25/29, which are about malformed input, not queue-full behavior).
